title: Biofunctionalized Prussian Blue Nanoparticles for Multimodal Molecular Imaging Applications
protocol: Prepare solution 'A' containing 5 ml of 5 mM potassium hexacyanoferrate (II) in DI water.
For PB NPs, prepare 10 ml of a solution containing 2.5 mM iron (III) chloride in DI water.
For GdPB NPs, prepare 10 ml of a solution containing 2.5 mM each of gadolinium (III) nitrate and iron (III) chloride in DI water.
For MnPB NPs, prepare 10 ml of a solution containing 2.5 mM each of manganese (II) chloride and iron (III) chloride in DI water.
Add solution ‘B’ to a round-bottom flask and stir at room temperature and 1,000 rpm.
Add solution ‘A’ drop-wise into the round-bottom flask containing solution ‘B’ using a peristaltic pump set to dispense approximately 10 ml/hr.
Continue stirring at 1,000 rpm for an additional 30 min after the addition of solution ‘A’ is complete.
Stop stirring and collect the mixture.
Transfer aliquots of the mixture into microcentrifuge tubes to rinse nanoparticles free of unreacted components.
Add 5 M NaCl (0.2 ml NaCl/ml reaction mixture) to each aliquot to assist in particle collection by centrifugation.
Centrifuge each aliquot of nanoparticles for at least 10 min at 20,000 × g.
Remove the supernatant carefully after centrifugation.
Resuspend each nanoparticle pellet in 1 ml DI water via sonication using a microtip with settings of pulse on/off = 1/1 sec, amplitude = 50%, duration = 5 sec, and sonicator power rating = 125 W.
Repeat steps for resuspending nanoparticles at least 3× to ensure removal of reaction components and byproducts.
Resuspend particles in 1 ml DI water after the final centrifugation.
Prepare suspensions of PB NPs, GdPB, or MnPB in 1 ml DI water.
Filter Alexa Fluor 488-labeled avidin (A488) through a 0.2 µm nylon microcentrifuge filter at 14,000 × g for 10 min.
Add ≤0.2 mg of filtered A488 per mg of nanoparticles to the nanoparticle suspensions.
Contact the nanoparticles with A488 for 2-4 hr with gentle shaking or rotation at 4 °C.
Protect the samples from light using aluminum foil during incubation.
Prepare suspensions of avidin-coated nanoparticles in 1 ml DI water.
Filter biotinylated antibody through a 0.2 μm nylon microcentrifuge filter at 14,000 × g for 10 min.
Add filtered aliquot of biotinylated antibody to the suspensions of avidin-coated nanoparticles.
Contact avidin-coated nanoparticles with biotinylated antibodies (ANG2 or Eot3) for 2-4 hr with gentle shaking at 4 °C.
Add 10 µl of the nanoparticle sample (1 mg/ml) to 990 µl of DI water in a disposable plastic cuvette.
Cap the cuvette and vortex to mix well.
Place the cuvette in a system used to analyze particle size at a measurement angle of 173°.
Add 100 µl of the nanoparticle sample (1 mg/ml) to 900 µl of DI water in a disposable plastic capillary cell.
Place the capillary cell in a system used to analyze zeta potential using default parameters at 25 °C.
Assess the stability of nanoparticles by measuring sizes in DI water as well as Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium (DMEM).
Repeat size measurements in DI water and DMEM once/day over a period of 5 days.
Seed 10,000-15,000 cells/well in a 96-well plate.
Ensure the total volume of seeded cells does not exceed 0.2 ml/well.
Incubate seeded cells overnight at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Incubate cells with varying concentrations of nanoparticles (0.01 – 0.5 mg/ml).
Add a blank consisting of appropriate nanoparticle concentration to medium without cells.
Aspirate media from each well after incubation.
Rinse cells with staining buffer comprised of 5% fetal bovine serum in PBS.
Add 100 µl of media without phenol red and incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 16-18 hours.
Prepare the XTT Cell Proliferation Assay working solution as per manufacturer’s specifications.
Aspirate the media from the wells after preparation.
Add 100 µl of RPMI or appropriate medium for the cell type studied to each well.
Add 50 µl of XTT working solution to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2-2.5 hours.
Measure the absorbance at 490 nm, with a reference wavelength of 630 nm to correct for fingerprints or smudges.
Calculate the corrected absorbance for each well (A490-A630).
Average the readings for replicates.
Subtract the blank readings from each well value to calculate the final corrected absorbance values.
Calculate the survival percentage for each sample by normalizing the final corrected absorbance to that of untreated cells without nanoparticles.
Plot survival percentage as a function of nanoparticle concentration.
Prepare a 96-well plate with each well containing 100 µl nanoparticles (PB NPs, GdPB, or MnPB) at the appropriate concentration.
Begin with a concentration of 0.4 mM for each type of nanoparticle.
Serially dilute the nanoparticles 2× using DI water until a concentration of 2.4 × 10-5 M is reached (this requires 14 dilutions and 15 wells).
Add 100 µl of molten 1% agarose solution in DI water into each well.
Mix well.
Allow the gel to solidify at 4 °C for 12 hr.
Place the phantom containing serial dilutions of nanoparticles in solidified agarose into a horizontal 3 T clinical magnet under a block of 2% agar (150 cm³).
Secure the phantom and block of agar within the center of an 8-channel HD brain coil.
Measure relaxation times using 0.5 mm thick coronal slices at the mid-height of the 96-well plate.

Acquire T1-weighted MR images using a fluid attenuated inversion recovery sequence with Echo train = 8, Repetition time = 2300 msec, Echo time = 24.4 msec, Matrix size = 512 x 224, Field of view = 16 x 16 cm².

Acquire T2-weighted MR images using a fast relaxation fast spin echo sequence with Echo train = 21, Repetition time = 3500 msec, Echo time = 104 msec, Matrix size = 512 x 224, Field of view = 16 x 16 cm².
Acquire T1W and T2W MR images at 127 MHz (3 T) at the following inversion times: 50, 177, 432, 942, 1961, and 4000 msec.
Measure signal intensity for each well using ImageJ by selecting the region of interest using the oval crop button located on the main toolbar.
Select Analyze > Measure to quantify the signal intensity.
Plot the measured signal intensity against its specific inversion time for each ROI.
Invert points that generate an initial “bubble” or outliers at the beginning of the plot.
Prepare an exponential fit for each plot of signal intensity versus inversion times.
Solve for T1 or T2 using the equation provided and plot the inverse values (1/T1 and 1/T2) against nanoparticle concentrations.
Calculate the slope of the linear graph to yield the relaxivities r1 and r2.
Dip no. 1.5 micro cover glasses in a solution of 0.002% poly(L-lysine) hydrobromide for 90 min.
Allow the covered glasses to dry for 24 hr.
Seed cells (e.g., EoL-1, BSG D10, SUDIPG1) on the coated cover glasses placed in a 6-well plate and incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for at least 16 hr.
Rinse the cells with a 1× PBS solution.
Fix the cells with 10% formaldehyde in neutral buffer solution for 15 min (optional).
Stain cells with 5 μM red-orange cell-permeant dye in PBS at 37 °C for 30 min.
Subsequently, rinse cells with PBS.
Add 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA; in DI water) to the cells and incubate at 37 °C for 1 hr.
Incubate cells with nanoparticles in 1% BSA for 1 hr.
For EoL-1: Incubate with 0.2 mg/ml GdPB-A488 or GdPB-A488-Eot3.
For BSG D10 and SUDIPG1: Incubate with 0.2 mg/ml MnPB-A488 or MnPB-A488-ANG2.
Rinse the cells with PBS three times to remove unbound nanoparticles.
Invert the cover glass containing cells and nanoparticles on a microscope slide carefully, ensuring no air bubbles are trapped.
Seal the edge between the cover glass and microscope slide using clear nail polish.
Image the cells using a confocal laser scanning microscope.
Prepare suspensions of targeted cells in PBS for pure culture studies with BSG D10 cells at 100,000 cells/ml (10 ml total).
Prepare suspensions of targeted cells in PBS for mixed culture studies with EoL-1 and OE21 cells at 100,000 cells/ml each (10 ml total).
Resuspend cell pellets of EoL-1 cells in PBS to make a ratio of 1:0 (2 ml EoL-1).
Mix 1.5 ml of EoL-1 and 0.5 ml of OE21 cells in PBS for a 3:1 ratio.
Combine 1 ml each of EoL-1 and OE21 cells in PBS for a 1:1 ratio.
Resuspend cell pellets of OE21 cells in PBS to make a ratio of 0:1 (2 ml OE21).
Mix 0.5 ml of EoL-1 and 1.5 ml of OE21 cells in PBS for a 1:3 ratio.
Block the cells with 2 ml of 5% BSA to minimize non-specific binding.
Add 1 ml (1 mg/ml) nanoparticles to the cells and incubate for 1 hr.
For BSG D10, incubate cells with MnPB-A488, MnPB-A488-AbC (control antibody), or MnPB-A488-ANG2.
Rinse the cells free of unbound nanoparticles by spinning down the samples at 1,000 × g for 5 min at least 3 times to remove unbound particles.
Resuspend the cells in 1 ml PBS and fix with 10% formaldehyde in PBS.
Stain cells by incubating with 10 µg/ml 7-Aminoactinomytcin D in PBS on ice for 30 min.
Rinse cells with PBS.
Analyze 10,000 gated cells from each sample using a flow cytometer.
Grow cells (e.g., BSG D10) in T75 flasks until ~80% confluence.
Use appropriate growth medium and conditions.
For BSG D10, grow the cells in DMEM + 10% FBS + 1× Pen-Strep at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Rinse cells free of medium with 5 ml PBS.
Block the cells with 5 ml 1% BSA in PBS for 1 hr to minimize non-specific binding.
Add 5 ml (0.5 mg/ml) nanoparticles to the cells.
For BSG D10, incubate the cells with MnPB-A488, MnPB-A488-AbC (control antibody), and MnPB-A488-ANG2 for 1 hr.
Rinse cells 3× with 5 ml PBS to remove unbound nanoparticles.
Incubate the cells with 2 ml Trypsin EDTA 0.25% solution for 5 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2 to detach them from the flask.
Add 8 ml of DMEM to quench the trypsinization of cells.
Centrifuge the cells at 1,000 × g for 5 min; aspirate out the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 ml PBS.
Add 100 µl of each sample to a separate well of a 96-well plate.
Add 100 µl of molten 1% agarose solution in DI water into each well and mix by pipetting up and down.
Allow the gel to solidify at 4 °C for 12 hr.
Place the phantom containing cells with attached nanoparticles in a horizontal 3 T clinical magnet next to a solid block of 2% agar (150 cm³).
Secure the phantom and block of agar within the center of an 8-channel HD brain coil.
Measure relaxation times using 0.5-mm thick coronal slices at mid-height of the 96-well plate.
Acquire T1W MR images using a spin echo sequence with Echo train (ET) = 1, Repetition time (TR) = 650 msec, Echo time (TE) = 11 msec, Matrix size = 320 x 256, and Field of view (FOV) = 10 x 10 cm².
Acquire T2W MR images using the FRFSE sequence.
Set ET = 28, TR = 3000 msec, TE = 101 msec, Matrix size = 384 x 288, FOV = 10 x 10 cm².
Convert original gray scale images into a color scale image using ImageJ.
Select Image > Type > 8-Bit to convert the image to grayscale.
Calculate the normalized intensity for each sample after subtracting the signal contribution from the agarose solution.
